column3: Close to the Greek; “authority” is rendered “power.”
NKJV reads “Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “Thaddaeus.”
NKJV puts “cleanse the lepers” before “raise the dead,” following the order of the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “raise the dead” first.
Close to the Greek; “take along” is rendered “provide.”
NKJV has the plural “staffs,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the singular. “Provisions” is rendered “food.”
Close to the Greek; “shrewd” is rendered “wise” and “innocent” as “harmless.”
Close to the Greek; “courts” is rendered “councils.”
NKJV spells the name “Beelzebub,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Beelzebul.” NKJV supplies “will they call.”
NKJV renders the coin “assarion” as “a copper coin” and adds “will” after “your Father’s.”
